headline: Last session: Sensex gained over 300 points as Indian markets recovered partially from sharp midweek losses.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 28 September.

why: Indian benchmarks rebounded on Friday after heavy midweek sell-offs driven by crude oil surging above $100.
Auto and consumer durables sectors saw buying interest, gaining nearly 1% during the last session.
Proposed insurance curbs and geopolitical oil spikes caused Thursday's sharp market crash where Nifty fell below 23,100.
Government's announcement to reduce FY27 borrowing by ₹1.2 trillion provided some fiscal relief to sentiment.
whatHappening: Indian stock markets ended lower for the week overall despite a partial rebound on Friday.
Government has begun evaluating financial bids for the strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank.
Zee Entertainment sought action against Reliance-Disney's JioStar regarding an alleged copyright breach.
Primary market activity remains active with JSW One Platforms filing draft papers for a ₹3,054 crore IPO.
summary:
Indian markets ended the week lower overall after facing a heavy sell-off on Thursday triggered by high crude oil prices.
Markets managed a partial recovery on Friday, with the Sensex gaining over 300 points supported by auto and consumer durables.
Trading remains closed today for the weekend and will resume on Monday, 28 September.
